args.sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT o.store_id, o.customer, COUNT(*) n FROM orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) customers, MEDIAN(n) med, quantile_disc(n,0.5) qd FROM c LEFT JOIN stores s ON c.store_id=s.id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE customer IS NULL), COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE store_id IS NULL) FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-01-01'

args.message: Based on 2025 orders (1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025). Each customer's orders were counted separately at each store they ordered from, so one customer can appear under more than one store. Brooklyn had the highest median at 167 orders per customer, across 701 customers. Los Angeles (median 24) and New Orleans (median 70) are low because they opened partway through 2025, in October and April. Their numbers cover only part of the year and aren't directly comparable to the other stores.
